Runs a checklist of common failure points: installed provider versions and unavailable-plugin reasons, each registered provider's own diagnostics, the configured assistant's native login, OpenCode runtime SDK and executable presence, database reachability, workspace writability, bundled defaults, folder-project detection (contained repos, when run from one), telemetry state, AI credentials connected in Archon, and adapter token pings (Slack/Telegram, best-effort). The AI credentials check uses each connected credential the way a database-store run would: it decrypts it and refreshes an expired subscription grant (saving the rotated grant only if the credential it refreshed is still stored). It prints one line per credential and fails when one cannot be used (it cannot be read, the vendor rejected the refresh, or the refresh replaced the refresh token and the new grant could not be saved), naming the command that reconnects it. It warns when a credential could not be verified, for example because the vendor was unreachable or a concurrent credential change superseded the refresh. Run doctor again to verify the replacement. An API key is reported usable once it decrypts; only a model request proves the vendor accepts it.

The assistant login check uses the merged configuration and the provider's own runtime, unless that model's vendor already has a credential connected in Archon that the assistant can use. Provider specifics:
Pi cannot use a connected Claude subscription: with no native Anthropic login, the check fails and names

When Archon config names no model (Pi then uses its own default), doctor cannot tell which vendor the run uses, so a missing native login is a warning, not a failure, if you have connected a credential the assistant can use. key command once when a node starts and uses that key for the whole node, so a short-lived token can expire before a long node ends; a model from an extension provider runs its key command on each request. Pi OAuth checks may refresh through Pi's runtime.

Codex reads its native account through app-server and asks it to refresh the sign-in (a turn does not make this call). If Codex reports no account, Archon rechecks once in a fresh process under the same deadline. The recheck still requests a refresh; a login that remains unavailable blocks the run. When the second read returns a status, the

event records the resulting credential state without account or token values. An API key is usable once resolved. When Codex is configured for a model provider that needs no OpenAI login, the check is skipped.
Claude reads account information through its SDK without sending a model request.
